key_insight: The paper introduces Agent-Guided Relational Concept Discovery, which learns interpretable concepts directly from REIMS data to improve surgical margin assessment without requiring concept labels.
engineering_relevance: It targets a key deployment gap in surgical AI by making models more robust to intraoperative noise while adding concept-level interpretability for clinical trust and debugging.
method: Learn concepts from unlabeled mass spectrometry spectra instead of relying on predefined annotations.
Use a reasoning agent to refine semantic descriptions of concepts and adjust their diagnostic importance during training.
Ground discovered concepts with a biochemical knowledge graph to align them with known metabolic relationships.
evidence_signal: Across Skin and Breast Cancer datasets, the model improves balanced accuracy and sensitivity over the baseline, and a representative intraoperative case shows fewer false positives.
watch_item: Concept grounding and agent-guided refinement may add system complexity and still require careful validation to ensure learned concepts remain clinically meaningful across sites and devices.
paper_title: Agent-Guided Relational Concept Discovery: Toward Interpretable Surgical Margin Assessment
